answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove a repeated, coordinated fraud under a published rule. Accounts that merely share an owner are not automatically punished; evidence must concern behavior, such as matching offers and circular trades. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it. An opal, marble, or yarrow account gains no special exemption.
